concepts.name: The Heron Gate
concepts.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Create ONE new original Olivia Arcana TAROT CARD BACK illustration. Portrait 7:12, flat straight-on full rectangular artwork, same proportion as the references, high detail. Input 1 (heron back) and input 2 (olive grove back) are the APPROVED visual direction; input 3 (Moon front) is the established deck's material reference. Use their lapis-blue carved stone, warm sculptural ivory and selective muted gold; invent the new composition described below. Elevate the drawing, precision of contours and organization of light and dark. The image should feel like an exquisitely observed shallow sculptural relief with fine chisel work, NOT a shiny CGI ornament or a generic AI fantasy image. ONE coherent relief system: broad quiet planes, delicate recessed cuts, fine high points, deep shadows only at overlap. Predominantly midnight and lapis blue, limited luminous warm ivory focal shapes, very few purposeful gold accents. Use the material grain quietly in coherent regions, not noisy distressed grit sprinkled everywhere. Olive leaves anatomically credible: slender lanceolate pointed forms, fine central vein, believable paired attachments to a tapering stem, naturally turning leaf surfaces. Elegant branch junctions; each important contour should lead somewhere. Clear dramatic silhouette from far away, fine botanical modelling close up. Keep generous deep-blue intervals so the imagery can breathe, richer carefully worked pockets elsewhere. Intended as a two-ended card back: compose a deliberate 180-degree rotational relationship with organic drawing within each half. Diffuse balanced illumination so both orientations feel natural. A narrow, quietly worn lapis perimeter only. No added frame or ornamental gold border. Output only artwork edge-to-edge; no surrounding space, mockup, perspective camera, table, room, lettering, numbers, title, logo, watermark. Avoid thick gold outlines, repeated decorative stock icons, sunbursts, zodiac wheels, medallions, jewel clutter, photographic blooms, neon, random stars, tangled impossible geometry, uniform plastic beveling.
COMPOSITION 06 — THE HERON GATE. Two exquisitely slender ivory herons create an elongated living gate: one sweeps up along the left side from lower-left toward upper-centre, the other is the rotational counterpart along the right side from upper-right toward lower-centre. Their poised S-curved necks, fine long beaks and compact overlapping wings describe a graceful continuous counterpoint. Each bird is fully credible and clearly distinct with one head, one body, correctly attached legs and elegant toes resting lightly on a small blue stone outcrop. The two long silhouettes frame a tall empty dark-blue almond-shaped interval at centre, containing ONLY one very small gold olive fruit as the quiet focal point. Blue-on-blue olive branches follow and partially cross behind the birds, then diverge into fine leaf clusters at upper-left and lower-right. Small areas of finely carved ivory wing feathers give tactile detail; much simpler smooth neck and breast surfaces let the shapes read. The balance of ivory to deep blue is approximately 30 to 70. This is a tall, lyrical, sculptural composition with rich figure-ground tension, not two birds beside a big round pond, not a heraldic badge. No pool rim, no halo, no circular ornament. The beauty comes from the interlocking silhouettes, precise bird anatomy and fine carving.

COMPOSITION 07 — THE VEIL OF LEAVES. A beautifully carved, narrow ivory cloth veil describes ONE broad languid S through the tall lapis field, with a half-turn symmetry: a gathered fold near upper-left flows inward then out toward lower-right, paired with the corresponding fold from the opposite end. Think of actual softly weighted fabric translated into shallow ivory carving, broad smooth luminous planes separated by a few very fine folded edges, not a ribbon rosette. A slender blue-stone olive bough emerges from behind each gathering of cloth and passes through a precise slit between two folds. The branches continue across the blue field in opposing arcs, carrying elegant sparse lanceolate leaves with finely modelled blue surfaces and a few ivory undersides. At the very centre the two cloth edges stop short, leaving a beautiful small lens of dark lapis, no object inside. Two restrained little gold olive fruit nestle at each cloth gathering. Extraordinarily fine drapery anatomy: every fold explains tension or gravity within its half. Relatively few leaves, exactly placed. At least half of the overall surface is quiet midnight lapis. No human, no architecture, no curtain rod, no gold frame. Poetic union of living branch and flowing fabric, sophisticated and tactile; the silhouette must feel drawn with great intent.

COMPOSITION 08 — THE OLIVE RELIQUARY. Two ancient olive trunks form a sculpted organic sanctuary within the stone: one rises from the lower-left and curves toward the upper-right; its inverted counterpart grows from the upper-right back toward the lower-left. Their broad worn blue wood surfaces twist gently, split into a few convincing tapering roots, and hold an elongated pool of almost-black blue at centre. Make the weathered trunks exquisitely sculptural: broad polished ridges next to fine grain cuts, recognisable organic wood anatomy translated into lapis stone, never spaghetti. A very delicate olive canopy grows at the two opposing ends, tiny paired leaves and elongated fruit, leaving the central inner edges largely bare and elegant. The two trunks meet the quiet water with small, fine ripples. Small pale-ivory mineral exposures lie inside selected trunk grooves, like the hidden heartwood, NOT gold branches everywhere. Exactly four small muted-gold olives near the negative-space opening supply precious highlights. The shape language has the gravitas of an ancient sculptural object, the restraint of fine botanical observation, and a dramatic almost-black sanctuary in the middle. Clear half-turn composition with large dark intervals. No rectangular architecture, no oval medallion rim, no bird, no face, no logotype. Much more emphasis on the magnificent trunk silhouette and surface carving than an all-over pattern of leaves.

COMPOSITION 09 — THE KEEPERS OF THE SPRING. A figurative shallow relief: TWO graceful ivory hands, each with a short draped wrist, enter from opposing diagonal corners as 180-degree counterparts. The first emerges from the upper-left edge, its palm gently cupped facing the viewer, holding one natural slender olive sprig. The second emerges from the lower-right edge as its inverted counterpart, also cupping a sprig. Hands are delicately observed classical sculpture: EXACTLY FIVE NATURAL FINGERS per hand including one thumb, correct joints, fine fingernails, no fused or extra digits, relaxed articulated pose. Keep all fingers readable. The two boughs bend toward each other around a deep-blue central spring, their leaves finely carved blue with a few ivory undersides and ONE gold olive in each palm. Below/behind the hands, very restrained blue stone bank contours and fine carved water ripples establish a single shared still space. The fingertips nearly meet the water but do not touch each other. Ivory modelling has smooth luminous skin planes, finely modelled knuckles; small cloth folds around wrists. The hands themselves are the striking large forms, beautifully silhouetted, surrounded by generous dark lapis. No face, full body, chalice, glowing orb, jewellery, nails painted gold, halo, radial flower, or ornamental border. Intimate, tender, mysterious, with the discipline of a carved classical relief and the warmth of the existing Star card.

COMPOSITION 10 — THE NOCTURNAL KNOT. Two slender olive boughs weave into one tall continuous sculptural knot, with a sophisticated 180-degree rotational design. Design a large, elegant asymmetrical-in-each-half S-shaped loop rather than a generic figure-eight infinity symbol. The two pale ivory stems have naturally tapering cross-sections and exactly TWO clear over-under crossings, fully believable physical continuity. Long spare lapis-blue olive leaves emerge in beautifully spaced groups and follow the direction of growth, with subtle ivory undersides on selected turned leaves. The branches open around one generous elongated dark-blue central space and two smaller side passages; that negative space is as carefully drawn as the stems. Four small elongated muted-gold olives act as pauses at the transitions of the curves. The knot is shallow, finely carved, exceptionally elegant, with the same rich dark mineral blue ground as the reference deck. Leaf veins and carving edges can be tiny and precise, but preserve a bold readable complete silhouette. Draw the branch routing with extraordinary care; no ends disappearing into nothing, no fused crossing, no impossible tangled loops. Quiet outer perimeter, plentiful deep blue, no circular frame, no isolated centre icon, no flower, no animal, no portrait. The whole olive composition is the identity: sculptural botanical calligraphy, alive and restrained, never a flat vector logo.
